parts.article:
The Significant Role of Mother Tongue in Education
 
(A) One consequence of population mobility is an increasing diversity within schools. To illustrate, in the city of Toronto in Canada, 58% of kindergarten pupils come from homes where English is not the usual language of communication. Schools in Europe and North America have experienced this diversity for years, and educational policies and practices vary widely between countries and even within countries. Some political parties and groups search for ways to solve the problem of diverse communities and their integration in schools and society. However, they see few positive consequences for the host society and worry that this diversity threatens the identity of the host society. Consequently, they promote unfortunate educational policies that will make the “problem” disappear. If students retain their culture and language, they are viewed as less capable of identifying with the mainstream culture and learning the mainstream language of the society.
 
(B) The challenge for educators and policy-makers is to shape the evolution of national identity in such a way that the rights of all citizens (including school children) are respected, and the cultural, linguistic, and economic resources of the nation are maximised. To waste the resources of the nation by discouraging children from developing their mother tongues is quite simply unintelligent from the point of view of national self-interest. A first step in providing an appropriate education for culturally and linguistically diverse children is to examine what the existing research says about the role of children's mother tongues in their educational development.
 
(C) In fact, the research is very clear. When children continue to develop their abilities in two or more languages throughout their primary school, they gain a deeper understanding of language and how to use it effectively. They have more practice in processing language, especially when they develop literacy in both. More than 150 research studies conducted during the past 25 years strongly support what Goethe, the famous eighteenth-century German philosopher, once said: the person who knows only one language does not truly know that language. Research suggests that bilingual children may also develop more flexibility in their thinking as a result of processing information through two different languages.
 
(D) The level of development of children's mother tongue is a strong predictor of their second language development. Children who come to school with a solid foundation in their mother tongue develop stronger literacy abilities in the school language. When parents and other caregivers (e.g., grandparents) are able to spend time with their children and tell stories or discuss issues with them in a way that develops their mother tongue, children come to school well-prepared to learn the school language and succeed educationally. Children's knowledge and skills transfer across languages from the mother tongue to the school language. Transfer across languages can be two-way: both languages nurture each other when the educational environment permits children access to both languages.
 
(E) Some educators and parents are suspicious of mother tongue-based teaching programs because they worry that they take time away from the majority language. For example, in a bilingual program when 50% of the time is spent teaching through children's home language and 50% through the majority language, surely children won't progress as far in the latter? One of the most strongly established findings of educational research, however, is that well-implemented bilingual programs can promote literacy and subject-matter knowledge in a minority language without any negative effects on children's development in the majority language. Within Europe, the Foyer program in Belgium, which develops children's speaking and literacy abilities in three languages (their mother tongue, Dutch and French), most clearly illustrates the benefits of bilingual and trilingual education (see Cummins, 2000).
 
(F) It is easy to understand how this happens. When children are learning through a minority language, they are learning concepts and intellectual skills too. Pupils who know how to tell the time in their mother tongue understand the concept of telling time. In order to tell time in the majority language, they do not need to re-learn the concept. Similarly, at more advanced stages, there is transfer across languages in other skills such as knowing how to distinguish the main idea from the supporting details of a written passage or story, and distinguishing fact from opinion. Studies of secondary school pupils are providing interesting findings in this area, and it would be worth extending this research.
 
(G) Many people marvel at how quickly bilingual children seem to “pick up” conversational skills in the majority language at school (although it takes much longer for them to catch up with native speakers in academic language skills). However, educators are often much less aware of how quickly children can lose their ability to use their mother tongue, even in the home context. The extent and rapidity of language loss will vary according to the concentration of families from a particular linguistic group in the neighborhood. Where the mother tongue is used extensively in the community, then language loss among young children will be less. However, where language communities are not concentrated in particular neighborhoods, children can lose their ability to communicate in their mother tongue within 2–3 years of starting school. They may retain receptive skills in the language but they will use the majority language in speaking with their peers and siblings and in responding to their parents. By the time children become adolescents, the linguistic division between parents and children has become an emotional chasm. Pupils frequently become alienated from the cultures of both home and school with predictable results.

Questions 27–30
Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.
Write the correct letter in boxes 27–30 on your answer sheet.

Q27 What point did the writer make in the second paragraph?

  • A Some present studies on children's mother tongues are misleading.
  • B A culturally rich education programme benefits some children more than others.
  • C Bilingual children can make a valuable contribution to the wealth of a country.
  • D The law on mother tongue use at school should be strengthened.

Q28 Why does the writer refer to something that Goethe said?

  • A to lend weight to his argument
  • B to contradict some research
  • C to introduce a new concept
  • D to update current thinking

Q29 The writer believes that when young children have a firm grasp of their mother tongue

  • A They can teach older family members what they learnt at school.
  • B They go on to do much better throughout their time at school.
  • C They can read stories about their cultural background.
  • D They develop stronger relationships with their family than with their peers.

Q30 Why are some people suspicious about mother-tongue-based teaching programmes?

  • A They worry that children will be slow to learn to read in either language.
  • B They think that children will confuse words in the two languages.
  • C They believe that the programmes will make children less interested in their lessons.
  • D They fear that the programmes will use up valuable time in the school day.

Q27

解析 题目问作者在第二段提出了什么观点。B段提到最大限度利用国家的文化、语言和“economic resources（经济资源）”符合国家利益，反之则是浪费。这对应选项 C：双语儿童能为国家财富做出宝贵贡献。

干扰 B段核心在于“national self-interest”和“economic resources”，即国家层面的利益，而非单纯对比某些儿童获益更多（排除B）。

句子 (Paragraph B) "...the cultural, linguistic, and economic resources of the nation are maximised... intelligent from the point of view of national self-interest."

Q28

解析 题目问作者为什么引用歌德（Goethe）的话。C段先提到“150多项研究强烈支持”歌德的观点。引用名言是为了给之前的论点（即研究结论）增加权威性或分量，对应选项 A（增加其论点的分量）。

干扰 引用名人名言在议论文中通常用于佐证观点（lend weight），而非反驳研究（排除B）或引入新概念（排除C，概念前文已述）。

句子 (Paragraph C) "More than 150 research studies... strongly support what Goethe... once said..."

Q29

解析 题目问当幼儿牢固掌握母语时，作者认为会怎样。D段提到带着“solid foundation（坚实基础）”母语入学的孩子，能“succeed educationally（在教育上取得成功）”，对应选项 B（在校期间表现得更好）。

干扰 “Succeed educationally” 对应 “do much better throughout their time at school”。A、C、D均为段落中未提及的具体结果。

句子 (Paragraph D) "Children who come to school with a solid foundation in their mother tongue... succeed educationally."

Q30

解析 题目问为什么有些人对母语教学项目持怀疑态度。E段开头提到他们担心这会“take time away from the majority language（占用主流语言的时间）”，对应选项 D（担心项目会占用宝贵的在校时间）。

干扰 “Take time away” 是核心担忧，直接对应 “use up valuable time”。

句子 (Paragraph E) "...because they worry that they take time away from the majority language."

Q31

解析 题目说双语儿童很快获得用主流语言交谈的____。G段提到他们似乎很快“pick up conversational skills（习得会话技巧）”，即获得了交谈的“ability（能力）”，选 I。

干扰 题目空格需要名词，“skills” 对应选项中的 “ability”。

句子 (Paragraph G) "...bilingual children seem to 'pick up' conversational skills..."

Q32

解析 题目说母语可能以相似的____消失这一事实不为人知。G段提到教育者往往没意识到孩子失去母语有多“quickly（快）”，以及语言流失的“rapidity（速度）”，对应选项 D（速率）。

干扰 “How quickly” 和 “rapidity” 都在描述速度，对应 “rate”。

句子 (Paragraph G) "...how quickly children can lose... The extent and rapidity of language loss..."

Q33

句子 (Paragraph G) "...concentration of families... in the neighborhood."

解析 题目说这取决于定居在特定____的同语言背景人群的比例。G段提到这取决于邻里（neighborhood）中家庭的集中度，对应选项 J（区域）。

干扰 “Neighborhood” 指具体的地理范围，选项中 “area” 是最佳同义替换。

Q34

干扰 原文是 “responding to their parents”，选项归纳为 “family”。

句子 (Paragraph G) "...in responding to their parents."

解析 题目说孩子可能不再使用母语，甚至对____也是如此。G段提到孩子在回应“parents（父母）”时也会使用主流语言，父母属于家庭，对应选项 F。

Q35

解析 题目说青少年会体验到一种____感。G段末尾提到语言隔阂变成了“emotional chasm（情感鸿沟）”，学生经常感到“alienated（被疏远/格格不入）”，对应选项 C（错位/混乱）。

干扰 “Alienated” 意味着与环境脱节，选项中 “dislocation（错位/脱节）” 含义最接近。

句子 (Paragraph G) "...linguistic division... has become an emotional chasm. Pupils frequently become alienated..."

Q36

句子 (Paragraph A) "...58% of kindergarten pupils come from homes where English is not the usual language..."

解析 题目说多伦多幼儿园不到一半的孩子以英语为母语。A段说“58%... English is not the usual language（58%英语不是常用语）”，意味着以英语为常用语的只有42%，确实少于一半，选 YES。

干扰 数学逻辑：非英语58% > 英语42%（less than half）。

Q37

解析 题目说研究证明在校学习东道国语言会对母语产生不利影响。D段和E段多次提到“Transfer across languages（语言间迁移）”是双向的，且“both languages nurture each other（两种语言互相滋养）”，并不是单纯的负面影响（“adverse effect”），选 NO。

干扰 原文强调互利（nurture each other），题目说有害（adverse effect），直接矛盾。

句子 (Paragraph D) "...both languages nurture each other..."

Q38

解析 题目说Foyer项目将被法国教育系统接受。原文E段只提到Foyer项目在“Belgium（比利时）”实施，并教授三种语言（含法语），未提及“法国教育系统”是否接受它，选 NOT GIVEN。

干扰 不要看到“French（法语）”就联想到“French education system（法国教育系统）”，地理位置不符且无相关计划信息。

句子 (Paragraph E) "...the Foyer program in Belgium... (their mother tongue, Dutch and French)..."

Q39

解析 题目说双语儿童比单语儿童更早学会看时间。F段只用看时间作为“概念迁移”的例子（不需要重新学），并没有比较双语和单语儿童谁学得“earlier（更早）”，选 NOT GIVEN。

干扰 比较级信息（earlier）在文中不存在。

句子 (Paragraph F) "Pupils who know how to tell the time... do not need to re-learn the concept."

Q40

解析 题目说双语儿童可以将一种语言中获得的阅读理解策略应用到另一种语言中。F段提到技能如“区分主旨和细节”存在“transfer across languages（跨语言迁移）”，选 YES。

干扰 “Reading comprehension strategies” 对应原文的 “distinguish the main idea... distinguishing fact from opinion”。

句子 (Paragraph F) "...there is transfer across languages in other skills such as knowing how to distinguish the main idea..."
